The question is whether clause 4.4 of the consumer protection regulation covers this extension as a 'renewal of an existing service'. The text of 4.4 is not among the clauses provided, so I cannot confirm or deny that it applies, and I cannot cite it.

The clauses I do have point the other way but do not settle the question. [tdra-cpr-v2-en:4.7.1] requires consent to pay for a service to rest on an opt-in with a positive affirmative action by the subscriber. [tdra-cpr-v2-en:4.7.3] says consent is not inferred from failing to opt out. Neither mentions any exception for renewals.

The facts say the bundle is fixed-term and non-recurring, it expired on day 7, and there is no new consent. That suggests the 95 AED extension would be a new purchase, not a continuation. Whether 4.4 creates an exception cannot be decided without its text.
Next step: retrieve the text of clause 4.4 and the definitions in 4.2 before the care agent applies the extension or charges 95 AED.
